summary:
This project challenges creators to develop an interactive Space Mission Design Game that bridges the gap between isolated theoretical learning and practical aerospace engineering. Designed for individuals or teams of up to four, the game enables participants to conceptualize, configure, and simulate a complete space mission from the ground up.
Players must navigate complex, real-world trade-offs by balancing ambitious scientific goals against strict constraints like budget, mass, power, data volume, and mission lifetime. By making strategic decisions regarding spacecraft architecture, instrument selection, launch vehicles, and orbital mechanics, participants experience firsthand how choices in one subsystem ripple across the entire mission. The resulting experience combines engaging gameplay mechanics, dynamic resource management, and robust performance evaluations to reward effective engineering collaboration and problem-solving.
details: Our project is a multiplayer browser game where teams of up to four design, build, and simulate a space mission from scratch. Players balance real-world trade-offs—like budget, mass, and power—while navigating space hazards in asymmetric team roles to see if their spacecraft succeeds. Built with React, TypeScript, Node.js, and WebSockets, it turns dry aerospace theory into fun, hands-on teamwork. Our goal is to help students learn real engineering problem-solving by balancing authentic physics with accessible gameplay
